text:
alex: quick heads-up — after flipping channel multiplexing + LL128 on the 8xA100 perf lab we see a regression on end-to-end latency for short sequences. KV cache warmup seems to blow up all-reduce wait time. attaching notes below

maria: ugh. do you have the perf trace? timeline or nvprof?

alex: timeline from perfview attached (summarized). main observation: a bunch of tiny all-reduces (~32KB chunks) serialize across channels during kv warmup, causing stalls that the scheduler doesn't hide. overall p50 latency +18% and p95 +32% on our chat benchmark.

pranay: could be kernel selector falling back to proto for small chunks? we saw proto pick when chunk_size < 64KB on LL128 in last rollout.

dmitri: sharing the snippet I ran to reproduce locally:

```
# repro script
export NCCL_ALGO=LL128
export NCCL_PROTO=LL
export REDWOOD_COMM_CHANNELS=4
./run_inference --gpus=8 --batch=1 --seq_len=64 --kv-prefetch=on --trace=timeline.json
```

and a trimmed part of the timeline (timestamps are relative ms):

```
00.0 compute: forward chunk 0 (0.8ms)
00.8 allreduce ch0 start (0.4ms)
01.2 allreduce ch1 start (0.5ms)
01.7 compute: wait (0.2ms)
01.9 allreduce ch2 start (0.45ms)
02.35 allreduce ch3 start (0.5ms)
02.85 compute resumes
```

That overlap looks poor — channels are launching staggered and compute waits between them.

maria: did you try increasing chunk size or reducing channel count?

alex: toggled REDWOOD_COMM_CHANNELS=2 — p95 improved ~12% but throughput dropped slightly for long sequences. Increasing chunk size to 128KB also helped but hurt memory for large models.

pranay: that suggests the tradeoff space we suspected: LL128 gives good single-op bandwidth but amplification of per-chunk latency for many tiny collectives. For KV warmup pattern (lots of tiny KV pops) we may want adaptive algo selection: if avg chunk < X then force algo=RING or proto=LL (experiment) or collapse channels.

sara: proposal: add a quick heuristic in the scheduler — sample last N batches' reduce sizes; if median_chunk_bytes < 48k then temporarily set REDWOOD_COMM_CHANNELS=1 and prefer NCCL_ALGO=RING for next M seconds. Also add a micro-benchmark at startup to classify model's kv-chunk distribution.

alex: I like that. short-term: let's push a patch to CI that runs the chat benchmark with channel=4 vs channel=1 and records per-op all-reduce latencies. CI run: https://ci.redwood/example/comm-warmup/1955

ci-bot: CI run queued: https://ci.redwood/example/comm-warmup/1955

dmitri: sharing a perf flamegraph link where you can see the narrow spikes lining up with allreduce calls: https://perf.redwood/trace/1955

maria: any concerns about toggling algo on the fly? need to ensure compatibility between replicas; we can't have different ranks using different algos.

pranay: correct — must be a global policy per job. scheduler can pick policy and broadcast to all workers at rollout time. we should ensure safe fallback: if algo not supported on hw, fallback to default.

alex: next steps: (1) add sampling probe to runtime (2) run CI comparisons channel=1/2/4 with kv-warmup trace and produce per-op histograms (3) implement scheduler flag to pick channel_count/algo per-job. I'll spin up tickets.

sara: and follow up — run the same test with quantized kernels; sometimes quantization shifts the chunk size distribution and changes the sweet spot.

alex: thanks everyone — I'll drop the summarized numbers here after CI completes. :thumbsup:
